title: Falling with linear drag
caption: The solution v = (g/k)(1 − e^{−kt}) starts with slope g and levels off at the terminal velocity g/k. Shown for g = 9.8 m s⁻² and k = 0.5 s⁻¹ (an illustrative k): v_t = 19.6 m s⁻¹, and after one time constant 1/k = 2 s the velocity has reached 12.4 m s⁻¹, 63% of v_t.
alt: Velocity against time curve rising from zero with initial slope 9.8 and levelling off at the terminal velocity of 19.6 metres per second.
description: Velocity v against time t for dv/dt = g − kv with g = 9.8 and k = 0.5 (illustrative values).
At t = 0 the velocity is 0 and the slope is g = 9.8 m s⁻²: the drag is zero, so the ball falls freely.
As v grows the drag kv grows, the slope falls, and v approaches the terminal velocity g/k = 19.6 m s⁻¹ (dashed line), where drag balances weight.
After t = 1/k = 2 s the velocity is 12.4 m s⁻¹, 63% of the way there.

checks.name: the initial gradient is g = 9.8 m s⁻²
